newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Stockholm airport looking into longer runway.
newsitem.headline: Stockholm airport looking into longer runway.

text.p: Stockholm's Arlanda airport is considering lengthening a runway to handle a fully loaded Boeing 747 freighter, an airport spokesman said on Tuesday.

Christer Holst, manager for Arlanda's cargo development, told Reuters the airport was toying with the idea of extending its 3,300 metre long runway to 3,900 metres, the length needed for a fully-loaded, Far East-bound freighter to take off.
Plans were in only very early stages, he added.
"This has to do with whether we are going to be more involved in cargo. At the moment we are building a new cargo area, and this is part of that question," he said.
He said the project would cost around 200 million crowns.
"So far it's just an idea, something we are only looking into," Holst said.
He said the airport had also spoken to several airlines about adding new freight operations to the airport, but declined to give any details.
"There are talks with two or three airlines," he said.
